findings.decompiled: if _status[0] > 1: stop / ... (iteration 0, 15 lines) / _13 = 0 / mem[8576] = 1 / while _13 + 1 != 256: ... _13 = mem[8576]; mem[8576] = mem[8576] + 1   |   while True: ... _111 = mem[1216]; mem[1216] = mem[1216] + 1; if _111 + 1 != 256: continue; stop   (x5 in one body)
findings.source: PreseededVotingEscrowDelegation.vy:816 for i in range(256); :1021 and :1033 for i in range(10); :455 for i in range(78); :781 for _token_id in _token_ids; :343 for i in range(513)
findings.issue: Every Vyper range loop is rotated: either its first iteration is peeled and printed before the loop (80 duplicated lines in preseed's first loop) with the test 'while _prev + 1 != N', where _prev is the counter before its increment, or it is 'while True' with 'if _prev + 1 != N: continue / break' at the bottom, repeated at each of the 5 exits of batch_cancel_boosts' body. The counters (mem[1216], mem[8576], mem[1312], mem[672], mem[416]) are memory words.
findings.rule: Recognise the do-while shape 'body; i = i + 1; if i != N: goto body' as one loop with its test, not by peeling an iteration: 'while i < N' (or i != N) with the increment at the end. 'p = i; i = i + 1; if p + 1 != N' is 'i = i + 1; if i != N'. When every path of a loop body ends with the same increment-and-test, it is the loop's step and condition, printed once.

findings.source: :114-116 name / symbol / base_uri: public(String[32] / String[128]); :556 concat(self.base_uri, ...)
findings.issue: Copies of a Vyper string from storage (length word at slot p, data at p+1...) to memory are printed as loops whose bound is hidden in an early return; the Solidity equivalent prints 'return Array(len=name.length, data=name[all])'. The storage variables stay stor4 / stor6 / stor8 / stor9 although the getters return them.
findings.rule: A loop writing mem[d + 32*i] = stor[p + i] for i from a start to a bound computed from the length word, with no other effect, is one copy line mem[d len 32*k] = stor[p len k] (k from the bound); a string at slot p with its data at p+1.. is one storage variable (named after the getter that returns it). Also call.data[calldata.size len n] is n zero bytes and 31 - (x - 1) % 32 is ceil32(x) - x.

findings.source: local variables (adjusted_balance, ddata, expiry_data, next_expiry, expiries, receiver...), internal-call arguments and the scratch of nested HashMap keys, all of which Vyper keeps at fixed memory addresses
findings.issue: Locals stay mem[N], so their meaning is hidden, the halves of a local are read as byte slices (mem[400 len 16] is uint128(ddata), mem[384 len 16] its high half), and the stores of internal-call arguments and HashMap key scratch are printed although nothing reads them (7 dead lines per iteration in batch_set_delegation_status).
findings.rule: A constant memory address accessed only as the 32-byte word at that address (and slices of it), whose ranges are not otherwise read, is a local variable: name it and print slices of it as Mask/shift of the variable (mem[a + 16 len 16] = uint128(mem[a]), mem[a len 16] = mem[a] >> 128). A store no later read can see is dead (the sha3 scratch at [128, 192) once the sha3 is folded into the mapping access).

findings.source: :803 _delegators: address[256] (the argument is copied to memory and each address checked)
findings.issue: Vyper 0.3.1 unrolls the copy and check of the 256 addresses in the bytecode (346 CALLDATALOADs in the code), and the text prints all 512 lines. Afterwards the loop reads mem[32 * mem[8576] + 384] instead of _delegators[i].

findings.function: set_base_uri(string), admin(), and every call to VOTING_ESCROW
findings.decompiled: def set_base_uri(string _new_base_uri) payable: revert  |  const admin = 0x6104c052610320516104e052610340516105005260606104c0a4565b600080fd  |  static call 0xa0daf467ac52ecf3071f7a028d5b2adc802b213d6104805160008112614b1557.balanceOf(...)
findings.issue: Corpus artifact, not a decompiler error: Vyper 0.3.1 reads immutables at CODESIZE - 64 + k, and this pre-deployment runtime has no data appended, so they read the last 64 bytes of the code itself (checked: VOTING_ESCROW = code[-64:-32], AUTHORIZER_ADAPTOR = code[-32:]). The garbage word has high bits set, so caller == AUTHORIZER_ADAPTOR is always false and set_base_uri folds to 'revert': its String[128] storage write (an implicit copy loop) cannot be reviewed. The call target is also printed as a 32-byte word, not as the 20-byte address the CALL uses.
findings.rule: For the corpus: append zero-filled immutable data to Vyper runtimes (or decompile codecopy(codesize - k) as an unknown constant). In the text: print a call target or address constant masked to 160 bits.
findings.verified: reading only (bytecode tail compared with the constants)

findings.source: Vyper's checked signed arithmetic and bool clamps; self.boost_tokens[_token_id] = token (whole struct written back)
findings.issue: Leftovers that a general rule removes: 'x or False'; a bool clamp printed as 'not x / 2'; the selector copied to mem[28] and never read; a store of a slot's own value; overflow-case disjuncts made dead by an earlier require (_percentage >′ 0 makes '_percentage != -1' true; block.timestamp < 2^255 makes 'block.timestamp >=′ 0' true); 10**77 printed in hex while 10**i prints as a power.
findings.rule: x or False == x; not (x / 2^k) == x < 2^k (print x == bool(x) for k = 1); drop a store of the value just read from the same slot when an earlier store on the path already made the call non-static; simplify a condition with the facts established by dominating requires; print a constant equal to 10**n as 10**n.

notes: Vyper 0.3.1: no per-function source in the pack; reviewed against the full source at its end. All 42 ABI functions and the fallback ('revert', no __default__) reviewed. Same code: transferFrom = safeTransferFrom(address,address,uint256) without the onERC721Received call; cancel_boost = the body of batch_cancel_boosts; the _burn_boost block is the same in burn, cancel_boost, batch_cancel_boosts, extend_boost and the three transfer functions; preseed's _create_boost block is create_boost's. Checked by disassembly: the onERC721Received check 'require _1 == 0x150b7a02 << 224' compares the whole 32-byte response, and so does the bytecode (pc 612-668: mload of the slice buffer's data word, unmasked, XOR with the method_id word), a Vyper 0.3.1 quirk the text shows faithfully. The 4128-byte zero / mem[5568 len 4128] _data argument is faithful (Vyper sends the full Bytes[4096] buffer). Loop count: 12 explicit (7 copies of _burn_boost's range(513) loop, batch_cancel_boosts', _uint_to_string's, batch_set_delegation_status', preseed's two) + 8 implicit (3 getter string copies and tokenURI's base_uri copy as whiles; tokenURI's two concats and safeTransferFrom's _data calldata copy as copy lines; the unrolled address[256] copy). set_base_uri's String[128] copy is unreachable in this bytecode (see the coverage finding) and not counted. No execution run: the one doubtful point (gas hoisting) cannot change an effect.
summary: Faithful on every path checked, and every loop is present; but Vyper's memory-resident locals and loop counters stay mem[N] (with concat(mem[N]) keys and byte-slice reads), range loops are peeled or rotated, storage string copies stay loops, two functions print the same 45-line tail twice, and the boost arithmetic is printed as 2-3K-character repeated expressions.
